REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - SEPTEMBER 22, 2016 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
COUNCIL CHAMBERS, BLOOMFIELD AVENUE AT 183RD STREET
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
SEPTEMBER 22, 2016, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS AT CERRITOS CITY HALL,
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Alex Kim, First Evangelical Church of
  Cerritos.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Cerritos VolunTeens Daniella Saadati, Emily
  Pan, and Angelina Cheng.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in
  attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Carol Chen
  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Naresh Solanki
  Mayor/Chair George Ray

5.  Presentations/Appointments

  The following Proclamations were presented:

  Lazy Dog Restaurant and Bar (Business Spotlight).

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Sally Havice, representing Greater Los Angeles County League of Latin American
  citizens spoke in opposition to Measure M.

  Michael Wong, representing Congresswoman Linda Sanchez, highlighted a
  special event being hosted by the Congresswoman. He submitted a document for
  the record entitled, "Our Family and Alzheimer's".

  Jay Gray spoke regarding a Facebook page and expressed concerns regarding
  survey feedback from City residents. He spoke in support of trimming
  Councilmember benefits. He also spoke regarding Redevelopment and the use of
  the General Fund.

  Scott Smith, Cerritos Regional Chamber of Commerce, invited the community to
  the Taste of the Region event.

  Anatha Ramachandran spoke regarding the Astor Museum agreement.

  Chris Tierheimer, 1st CEB Adoption Committee, invited the community to the
  upcoming Meritorious Marine ceremony.

  City Clerk Barone announced that written correspondence regarding enforcement
  of commercial trucks on Marquardt Ave. was received from Ritu Gupta.
 City of Cerritos  September 22, 2016

7.  Consent Calendar
  Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by
  one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a
  Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item will be
  removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

7A.  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of
  September 8, 2016 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Chen, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of September 8, 2016
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY). The motion carried (4 – 0, 1 abstention -
  Solanki) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  Solanki

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated September

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Chen, to approve the Register
  of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated September 22, 2016 in the amount of
  $7,404,109.16 (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Approval of the Register of Demands for the Successor Agency to the Cerritos

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Chen, to approve the Register
  of Demands for the Successor Agency to the Cerritos Redevelopment Agency

  AGENCY).The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  AMENDING SECTION 22.22.700(15) AND SECTION 22.74.300 OF THE CERRITOS
  MUNICIPAL CODE ADDING REGULATIONS AND REQUIREMENTS FOR THE

  *Waiver of full reading approved at introduction of ordinance on September 8,

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Chen, to adopt Ordinance
  No. 1007, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS AMENDING

  ABSTAIN:  None

  1. Receive and file the 2016 Local Agency Biennial Notice; and
  2. Direct the City Clerk’s Office to present any proposed changes to the codes for

  job sites throughout the City of Cerritos, to Robertson’s Ready Mix, for a term of

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Chen, to

  1. Award a contract for Bid No. 1262-17, Annual Mechanical Equipment

  in the amount of $86,234, and reject all other bids received; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any change orders related

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Review and consideration of potential budget expenditure reduction measures
  (COUNCIL).

  Pursuant to City Council consensus, Public Hearing Items 8A and 8B were
  considered concurrently.

  A staff report was given by Ryan Carey. A PowerPoint Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments.

  George Shy expressed support for a community survey and opposition for an increase
  in sales tax.

  Katherine Chu opposed the sales tax increase, cuts to public safety services, and
  closure of any parks or community services.

  Sherman Kappe supported allowing the residents to vote on a potential sales tax
  increase to continue supporting the level of services and quality of life the City
  provides.

  Sally Havice spoke in opposition to the sales tax measure or any cuts to public safety.

  Rosalie Barber expressed concerns regarding cutting the public safety and the
  increase in homeless in the community.

  Rich Barber expressed concerns regarding cutting the public safety program.

  Jay Gray expressed concerns with the proposed budget reductions in community
  services and the expenditure of general fund money for redevelopment purposes.

  Anantha Narayanan spoke regarding increases in the current budget and proposed
  exiting the Magnolia Power Plant, proposing a ten percent cut across the board,
  privatizing the Performing Arts Center, eliminate the COW program, and looking into
  bond measures.
 City of Cerritos  September 22, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 9

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8A.  (continued)

  Ram Kakkar expressed concerns with the pension deficit, costs related to the
  Performing Arts Center, and the extensive services provided by the Cerritos Sheriff’s
  Station.

  Celia Spitzer suggested allowing the residents to vote on a proposed sales tax
  increase and suggested a sunset clause of five or ten years, which gives the
  opportunity to reevaluate the fiscal status of the City.

  Elaine Shiohama expressed support for the proposed budget cuts and in opposition to
  a proposed sales tax measure.

  Ephraim Baca expressed support for the proposed sales tax measure.

  William Mayfield expressed discontent with the way money has been spent in the
  City and expressed his support for public safety, but not at excessive levels.

  Hugo Encito encouraged the Council to consider outsourcing services, privatizing
  the Performing Arts Center, to be more business-oriented, and basing public safety
  on volume.

  Ernie Nichii spoke in opposition to a sales tax measure and encouraged the Council
  to make the decisions to balance the budget.

  Marlene Rofe made several suggestions related to various budget items eliminated
  certain giveaways and Commissions, scaling back certain employee events, and
  exiting the utility business. She submitted a document for the record.

  Chris Tierheimer spoke in support of the City Council and City Manager and for the
  sales tax measure. He expressed concerns regarding an outside operator that
  would bring in questionable acts to the Perfoming Arts Center. He also spoke in
  support of keeping the Cerritos Sheriff’s Station.

  Gail Swenson, Board member at Su Casa, thanking the Council for the financial
  support they currently provide for domestic violence protection services and the
  impacts of any reduction in financial support.

  David Forward reminded the community regarding Gold Star Mother's Day. He
  spoke in opposition to the museum and any proposed sales tax increase and
  requested consolidation of the City’s election with the County.

  Mark Bollman expressed concerns with misinformation in the community and
  expressed support for the enhanced quality of life services provided in Cerritos
  and placing a proposed sales tax measure on the upcoming ballot.

  Jay Gray expressed concerns and opposition to a proposed sales tax measure.
  He also expressed support for the Council to cut their own benefits prior to
  cutting resident services.

  Gavin Riley supports the existing enhanced City services and the proposed sales
  tax measure to continue them.
 City of Cerritos  September 22, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 6 of 9

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8A.  (continued)

  Clarence Stephens expressed support for the one-percent sales tax measure
  and in support of keeping the Cerritos Sheriff’s Station.

  Dan Usury expressed support for the Cerritos Sheriff’s Station and concerns
  with running up debt and liabilities. He encouraged a Town Hall meeting for the
  Council to dialogue with the residents and further analysis of the museum.

  Dixie Primosch commented regarding the various proposed cuts including
  exiting the Magnolia Power Plant, subleasing the Performing Arts Center,
  eliminating the stipends for Commissions and Committees, and privatizing
  certain services.

  The Mayor mentioned there was written correspondence received from Kelli
  Colewell and Clarence Stephens and from Ram Kakkar.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  public comments and the public hearing.

  CONSENSUS (Chen): Directed staff to bring back options regarding a Request for
  Proposals for operating the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts or leasing the
  facility.

  CONSENSUS (Chen): Directed staff to provide options to exit the electric utility.

  CONSENSUS (Chen): Directed staff to provide options for moving the upcoming
  general municipal election to a future date.

  MOTION: It was moved by Ray, and seconded by Pulido, to cut retirement benefits
  for future City Council members (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  MOTION: It was approved by unanimous consent to continue this item to the
  October 27, 2016 City Council/Successor Agency regular meeting (COUNCIL). The
  motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  CONSENSUS (Chen): Directed staff to provide information at the October 27, 2016
  meeting on impacts to the revenue streams of cities who have implemented a
  transactions tax.

  CONSENSUS (Solanki): Directed staff to bring back a report at the October 27,
  2016 meeting regarding a community survey.
 City of Cerritos  September 22, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 7 of 9

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8B.  Review and consideration of a proposal for the development of a ballot
  measure that would place before the Cerritos electorate at the March, 2017
  General Municipal Election the question of whether to approve a local sales tax
  increase (COUNCIL).

  Pursuant to City Council consensus, Public Hearing items 8A and 8B were
  considered concurrently. See Item 8A for public comments and other detail.

  MOTION: It was moved unanimous action to continue this item to the October 27,
  2016 City Council/Successor Agency regular meeting (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9A.  Review and consideration of award of a contract for Bid No. 1272-17, Cerritos

  A staff report was given by Kanna Vancheswaran, Director of Public Works.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to

  MOTION: It was moved by Chen, and seconded by Pulido, to continue this item to

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

(continued on next page)
 City of Cerritos  September 22, 2016

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the

10B1. Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt a resolution of the

  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Gerard Wright, MoveLA, spoke in support of Measure M.

  Noting there were no individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed public
  comments.
 City of Cerritos  September 22, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 9 of 9

10.  Legislative Items (continued)

10C.  (continued)

  1. Approve of the City’s participation in the Public Information Program through the

  The motion carried (4 – 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  Pulido
  ABSENT:  None
